notes: CBTRN01C, CardDemo's daily transaction validation: no JCL in the corpus runs it, so job and step are null and the DDs are its SELECTs' (DALYTRAN, CUSTFILE, XREFFILE, CARDFILE, ACCTFILE, TRANFILE). Each of CardDemo's daily transactions is DISPLAYed, its card looked up in the cross reference and its account read; every file is opened INPUT and none is written, so SYSOUT, RETURN-CODE and the abend are the outputs compared. CUSTFILE, CARDFILE and TRANFILE are opened and closed but never read. TRANFILE is the TRANSACT KSDS loaded as the corpus's TRANFILE.jcl STEP15 loads it (IDCAMS REPRO of the DALYTRAN initial file, dailytran.txt). At end of file the loop body still runs the lookups once more with the last transaction's card (the program's defect: SYSOUT shows the last transaction's xref and account reads twice). Every input is the corpus's data. Derived from CardDemo (Apache-2.0; Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates): LICENSE and NOTICE here are the source's own.

faults.name: dalytran-read-error
faults.why: 30: permanent I/O error (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values) on the third daily transaction: 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT -> ABEND U0999

faults.name: dalytran-early-end
faults.why: 10: end of file (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values) after two transactions: the second one's card and account are looked up again (the program's defect) and the step ends normally

faults.name: dalytran-empty
faults.why: 10: end of file on the first READ (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): the loop body still looks up DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM, which no READ has set (a WORKING-STORAGE item without VALUE: GnuCOBOL's spaces, shown in the message) -- INVALID KEY, 'COULD NOT BE VERIFIED' (the program's defect) -- and the step ends normally

faults.name: dalytran-status-9
faults.why: 9x: implementor-defined condition (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS's non-numeric / 9 arm, then ABEND U0999

faults.name: card-not-found
faults.why: 23: no cross reference for the first card (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): INVALID KEY in 2000-LOOKUP-XREF, the transaction is skipped -- the step goes on

faults.name: xref-read-error-stale
faults.why: 30 on the second cross-reference READ (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): no INVALID KEY and no status test, so the second transaction's account is read with the FIRST one's XREF-ACCT-ID (the program's defect) -- the step goes on

faults.name: account-not-found
faults.why: 23: no account for the first transaction (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): INVALID KEY in 3000-READ-ACCOUNT, 'ACCOUNT ... NOT FOUND' -- the step goes on

faults.name: account-read-error-silent
faults.why: 30 on the first account READ (IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS Language Reference, File status key values): neither INVALID KEY phrase runs and nothing tests the status, so the failed read goes unreported (the program's defect) -- the step goes on
